claim: The change modifies the decimal wire format in StandardClassLibraryFormatter by passing StandardFormat('F') to Utf8Formatter.TryFormat. This has nothing to do with REQ-2297, which is about attributes on generated code. With no explicit precision, the 'F' format is believed to use a fixed default number of fractional digits (2) instead of the round-trip 'G' form. If so, decimals such as 1.2345m would serialize as "1.23", silently losing data, and the bytes written for many decimal values would change.

Then deserialize the head bytes and assert each round-trips to the original value; expect 1.2345m to come back as 1.23m on head.

claim: The requirement says all generated code gets the attribute. Every emitted attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no attribute at all. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists on both targets (netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+) and allows AttributeTargets.Class there, so the guard is unnecessary. It leaves a large class of projects without the requested behaviour.

claim: The decimal formatter now passes StandardFormat('F') with no precision to Utf8Formatter.TryFormat. For 'F', Utf8Formatter defaults to 2 fractional digits, so serialized decimals are rounded. For example, 1.2345m is written as "1.23" and 0.001m as "0.00", which deserializes to 0. Scale also changes: 1.5m is written as "1.50" instead of "1.5". This silently corrupts data. The change is unrelated to REQ-2297 and alters the wire format.

claim: DecimalFormatter.Serialize now passes StandardFormat('F') to Utf8Formatter.TryFormat. The default format for decimal is 'G', which can emit exponent notation or differ from 'F' for some values (e.g. very small values or values with trailing zero scale). This changes serialized bytes for decimals, unrelated to the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage requirement. Existing users and peers reading stored or on-the-wire data would see different strings. 'F' also has different max length behavior (a 28-digit decimal with sign and point can exceed MaxFixStringLength 31?), so TryFormat may fail and fall to a different path.

claim: The attribute is emitted under #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, but the generated code is compiled in the user's project.
